# @moku-labs/native — Full LLM Reference

> Node-only native packager framework for Moku, built on @moku-labs/core (Layer 2). It
> generates a gitignored Tauri 2 project under `projectDir` (default `.moku/tauri`),
> codegens the permission surface (Tauri capabilities JSON, the Info.ios.plist sidecar,
> AndroidManifest needs) from whichever system plugins the consumer app composed in
> `config.system`, and drives `tauri build` / `tauri ios|android build` for five targets:
> macos, windows, linux, ios, android. Package manager: bun exclusively. A real `node`
> binary on PATH is a hard prerequisite (`@tauri-apps/cli` cannot run under bun).

Version: 0.1.0. Dependencies: @moku-labs/common 0.3.0, @moku-labs/core 1.5.0, @tauri-apps/cli ^2.
Node >= 24, Bun >= 1.3.14. TypeScript strict with exactOptionalPropertyTypes and noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

Table of contents:
1. Architecture and initialization order
2. Global Config + Events (src/config.ts — verbatim types)
3. Config schema (every field: type, default, description)
4. Complete event catalog
5. project plugin (types + behavior)
6. tauri plugin (types + behavior)
7. build plugin (types + behavior)
8. doctor plugin (types + behavior)
9. cli plugin (types + behavior)
10. Public exports (src/index.ts)
11. Usage examples (incl. the two-createApp consumer composition)
12. Error handling patterns
13. Extension patterns (custom plugins)
14. Key design decisions

====================================================================
1. ARCHITECTURE AND INITIALIZATION ORDER
====================================================================

Three-layer Moku model:
- Layer 1 — src/config.ts: `createCoreConfig<Config, Events, [typeof logPlugin, typeof envPlugin]>("native", { config: defaultConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] })`. The two @moku-labs/common core plugins put `ctx.log` (structured logging, MC2) and `ctx.env` (validated env access, MC3) on every plugin context.
- Layer 2 — src/index.ts: `createCore(coreConfig, { plugins: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin, cliPlugin], pluginConfigs: {...} })`.
- Layer 3 — consumer: `createApp({ config, plugins?, pluginConfigs? })` returns an app with `start()`/`stop()`, every plugin API surface (`app.project`, `app.tauri`, `app.build`, `app.doctor`, `app.cli`), and the core APIs.

Plugin dependency graph (D-007) and registration/initialization order:

  Wave 1 (dependency-free):   project        tauri
                                 ^  ^          ^  ^
  Wave 2:            build ------+--+----------+  |
                     doctor -----+-----------------+
                       ^  ^        (build -> [project, tauri])
                       |  |        (doctor -> [project, tauri])
  Wave 3:            cli -> [project, tauri, build, doctor]

Registration order in src/index.ts: project, tauri, build, doctor, cli.
- project and tauri never call each other; build orchestrates them; doctor reads them; cli fronts all four via ctx.require.
- Only project has an onInit (composition-time global-config validation — single owner).
- No plugin has onStart/onStop. tauri deliberately has NO onStop (D-002): a regular plugin's onStop receives only `{ global }` (no state/require/core APIs), so dev teardown is owned by the dev seam's own control flow (process-group spawn, SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, DevHandle.stop()) — which also covers Ctrl-C, where onStop would never fire.

Subprocess-seam ownership: tauri is the ONLY plugin that spawns processes for @tauri-apps/cli. doctor has its own `probeImpl` seam for non-tauri binaries (rustup/node/xcodebuild/java/...), but its one tauri-CLI probe goes through `tauri.version()` (D-013 ownership boundary).

====================================================================
2. GLOBAL CONFIG + EVENTS (src/config.ts — verbatim)
====================================================================

/** The five packaging targets (D1 — all five in v1). */
export const TARGETS = ["macos", "windows", "linux", "ios", "android"] as const;

/** A native packaging target. */
export type Target = (typeof TARGETS)[number];

/** Pipeline phases in execution order — drives NativePhase and progress rendering. */
export const PHASE_ORDER = [
  "scaffold",
  "codegen",
  "icons",
  "compile",
  "bundle",
  "collect"
] as const;

/** A build pipeline phase. */
export type NativePhase = (typeof PHASE_ORDER)[number];

/**
 * Per-capability packaging parameters — ONE map drives both `Config["capabilities"]`
 * and project's `resolve<K extends keyof CapabilityConfigMap>`.
 * deep-link is custom-scheme-only in v1 (D-011); the `mode` discriminant keeps `"universal"` additive later.
 */
export type CapabilityConfigMap = {
  store: Record<string, never>;
  notification: Record<string, never>;
  "clipboard-manager": Record<string, never>;
  tray: Record<string, never>;
  "deep-link": { mode: "scheme"; scheme: string };
};

/** Signing configuration — env-var REFERENCES and config-safe identifiers only, never raw secrets. */
export type SigningConfig = {
  android?: { keystorePath?: string; keystorePasswordEnv?: string; keyAlias?: string };
  windows?: { certificateThumbprint?: string };
};

/** Global configuration shape for the framework. Read by every plugin via `ctx.global`. */
export type Config = {
  /** App identity — project.onInit validates name/identifier are non-empty (reverse-DNS identifier). */
  app: { name: string; identifier: string; version?: string };
  /** Web build/dev wiring codegenned into tauri.conf.json. cwd for monorepo layouts. */
  web: { build: string; dev: { command: string; url: string }; dist: string; cwd?: string };
  /** Composed `@moku-labs/system` plugins — the kernel-guaranteed name-only contract. */
  system: ReadonlyArray<{ name: string }>;
  /** Per-capability packaging parameters. */
  capabilities: Partial<CapabilityConfigMap>;
  /** Targets this app ships (D1 default: all five). */
  targets: readonly Target[];
  /** Generated Tauri project root (contains src-tauri/). Gitignored build output. */
  projectDir: string;
  /** Installer delivery root. */
  outDir: string;
  /** Signing env-var references. */
  signing: SigningConfig;
};

/** native:phase payload — one flat event, target as a field. */
export type NativePhaseEvent = {
  target: Target;
  phase: NativePhase;
  status: "start" | "progress" | "done" | "error";
  durationMs?: number;
  detail?: string;
};

/** native:complete payload — where the shippable artifacts landed. */
export type NativeCompleteEvent = {
  target: Target;
  outPath: string;
  artifacts: readonly string[];
  durationMs: number;
};

/** Framework-level events — emitted by build, hookable by all plugins (D-003). */
export type Events = {
  "native:phase": NativePhaseEvent;
  "native:complete": NativeCompleteEvent;
};

Framework default config literal (src/config.ts):

const defaultConfig: Config = {
  app: { name: "", identifier: "" },
  web: {
    build: "bun run build",
    dev: { command: "bun run dev", url: "http://localhost:5173" },
    dist: "dist"
  },
  system: [],
  capabilities: {},
  targets: TARGETS,
  projectDir: ".moku/tauri",
  outDir: "dist-native",
  signing: {}
};

src/config.ts also exports `coreConfig`, and the JSDoc-surviving explicit re-exports:
`export const createPlugin = coreConfig.createPlugin;`
`export const createCore = coreConfig.createCore;`

====================================================================
3. CONFIG SCHEMA (field-by-field)
====================================================================

GLOBAL Config (D-005 — the substantive surface; every plugin reads it via ctx.global):

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| app.name | string | "" | Display name. Required: project.onInit throws when empty. |
| app.identifier | string | "" | Reverse-DNS bundle identifier (e.g. "com.example.myapp"). Validated against /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/i. |
| app.version | string? | (absent) | Optional app version, informational artifact context. |
| web.build | string | "bun run build" | Command that builds the web assets (codegenned into tauri.conf.json beforeBuildCommand wiring). Required non-empty. |
| web.dev.command | string | "bun run dev" | Command that starts the web dev server. Required non-empty. |
| web.dev.url | string | "http://localhost:5173" | Dev server URL — also the DevHandle.url and the readiness-poll target. Required non-empty. |
| web.dist | string | "dist" | Web build output directory (frontendDist). Required non-empty. |
| web.cwd | string? | (absent) | Working directory for the web commands — monorepo layouts. doctor's web-script check honors it. |
| system | ReadonlyArray<{ name: string }> | [] | The composed system plugins — the shared cross-team contract. Unknown names throw at composition time. |
| capabilities | Partial<CapabilityConfigMap> | {} | Per-capability packaging parameters. "deep-link" in `system` REQUIRES capabilities["deep-link"] = { mode: "scheme", scheme } with a non-empty scheme. |
| targets | readonly Target[] | all five | Targets this app ships. Default scope for build.runAll and doctor.run. |
| projectDir | string | ".moku/tauri" | Generated Tauri project root (contains src-tauri/). GITIGNORED build output, fully regenerable, never committed. |
| outDir | string | "dist-native" | Installer delivery root; collect copies artifacts to outDir/<target>/. |
| signing.android.keystorePath | string? | (absent) | Path to the release keystore (config-safe identifier). |
| signing.android.keystorePasswordEnv | string? | (absent) | NAME of the env var holding the keystore password — a reference, never the secret. |
| signing.android.keyAlias | string? | (absent) | Key alias inside the keystore. |
| signing.windows.certificateThumbprint | string? | (absent) | Windows signing certificate thumbprint. |

PER-PLUGIN configs (minimal knobs/seams; overridable via createApp({ pluginConfigs })):

tauri (src/plugins/tauri/types.ts):
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| spawnImpl | SpawnFn \| undefined | undefined | Injectable spawn for tests; undefined => real detached process-group spawn. |
| nodePath | string \| undefined | undefined | Explicit node binary path; undefined => PATH-walk resolution (never process.execPath, which is bun). |
| readiness | { intervalMs: number; timeoutMs: number } | { intervalMs: 250, timeoutMs: 60_000 } | dev()'s devUrl poll cadence — no stdout "ready" marker exists (tauri#4740), polling is the only readiness signal. |

doctor (src/plugins/doctor/types.ts):
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| probeImpl | ProbeFn \| undefined | undefined | Injectable probe runner for tests; undefined => real which/--version subprocess probes. The one tauri-CLI probe goes through tauri.version() instead (D-013). |

cli (src/plugins/cli/types.ts):
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| renderImpl | RenderFn \| undefined | undefined | (line: string) => void render sink for tests; undefined => branded console (@moku-labs/common/cli createBrandConsole). |
| confirmImpl | ConfirmFn \| undefined | undefined | (question: string) => Promise<boolean> for tests; undefined => styled branded confirm (gates cli.clean() without a target — full projectDir wipe). |

project and build have NO per-plugin config — they consume global config only.

====================================================================
4. COMPLETE EVENT CATALOG
====================================================================

GLOBAL framework events (declared in src/config.ts Events — D-003). Emitted by build;
hooked by cli; hookable by ANY plugin without a depends edge:

"native:phase" — payload NativePhaseEvent:
  { target: Target;
    phase: "scaffold" | "codegen" | "icons" | "compile" | "bundle" | "collect";
    status: "start" | "progress" | "done" | "error";
    durationMs?: number;   // present on done/error
    detail?: string }      // progress ticks ("Compiling <crate> [i/total]"), skip reasons ("skipped"), error text
  Emission pattern per phase: "start" -> zero or more "progress" (compile only, one per parsed
  crate tick — real cargo counts, never a synthesized percentage) -> "done" | "error".
  After an "error", NO further phase events fire for that run (the pipeline stops); "bundle"
  is never emitted at all when compile fails (the shared subprocess failure is attributed to compile).
  The icons phase always reports status "done" with detail "skipped" in v1 (D-015).

"native:complete" — payload NativeCompleteEvent:
  { target: Target; outPath: string; artifacts: readonly string[]; durationMs: number }
  Emitted once per successful build.run(), after collect. outPath = outDir/<target>/.

PER-PLUGIN event (declared by doctor via the register callback; hooking requires a
depends: [doctorPlugin] edge for event-type merging):

"doctor:check" — payload CheckResult:
  { id: string;
    target: Target | "host";
    status: "pass" | "warn" | "fail";
    message: string;       // human line, [native]-prefixed
    fixIt?: string }       // actionable next command/step
  Emitted once per completed check during doctor.run(). cli renders these live.

cli declares NO events — hooks only. Its hook map (handlers.ts):
  "native:phase"    -> updates ctx.state.progress bookkeeping (phase/startedAt/ticks) and renders a status line
  "native:complete" -> renders the completion box panel (app name, target, artifact paths, duration)
  "doctor:check"    -> renders the live pass/warn/fail row

====================================================================
5. PROJECT PLUGIN (Complex tier — src/plugins/project/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: owns the generated Tauri project as FILES — capability registry,
all generators for projectDir (tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml, src/main.rs + src/lib.rs,
capability JSON, the Info.ios.plist sidecar seam), the write-if-changed content-hash
writer, the mobile completeness gate, the Android signing patch pass, and clean.
It NEVER spawns subprocesses. Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, registry.ts, writer.ts,
completeness.ts, patch.ts, clean.ts, generators/{tauri-conf,cargo,rust,capabilities,sidecar,types}.ts.

Types (src/plugins/project/types.ts — verbatim):

/** Result of a write-if-changed generation pass. */
export type GenerateResult = { written: string[]; unchanged: string[]; skipped: string[] };

/** Mobile gen/-tree gate — completeness (required-file set), not existence. */
export type CompletenessResult =
  | { status: "not-applicable" }
  | { status: "not-initialized" }
  | { status: "incomplete"; missing: readonly string[] }
  | { status: "complete" };

/** Result of the idempotent mobile patch pass (v1: Android signing only). */
export type PatchResult = { patched: string[]; unchanged: string[] };

/** Result of a clean pass. */
export type CleanResult = { removed: readonly string[] };

/** One capability registry row — packaging metadata with per-row research confidence. */
export type RegistryRow = {
  name: keyof CapabilityConfigMap;
  npmPackage: `@tauri-apps/plugin-${string}`;
  crate: `tauri-plugin-${string}`;
  crateRange: string;
  npmRange: string;
  rustInit: string;
  permissions: readonly string[];
  platforms: readonly Target[];
  confidence: "high" | "medium" | "low";
};

/** A tauri.conf.json contribution fragment (plugins section + bundle metadata). */
export type TauriConfFragment = Record<string, unknown>;

/** An Info.ios.plist sidecar entry (src-tauri root, outside gen/) — empty for every v1 row. */
export type PlistEntry = { key: string; value: string };

/** An AndroidManifest need — empty for every v1 row (official plugins self-merge via build.rs). */
export type ManifestEntry = { parentTag: string; xml: string };

/** A capability resolved against consumer config. */
export type ResolvedCapability = RegistryRow & {
  conf: TauriConfFragment;
  sidecarPlist: readonly PlistEntry[];
  manifest: readonly ManifestEntry[];
};

/** Domain context — this plugin has no per-plugin config/state; global + log only. */
export type ProjectContext = {
  readonly global: Readonly<Config>;
  readonly log: LogApi;
};

/** Public API of the project plugin. */
export type Api = {
  generate(opts: { target: Target }): Promise<GenerateResult>;
  completeness(opts: { target: Target }): CompletenessResult;
  patchMobile(opts: { target: "ios" | "android" }): Promise<PatchResult>;
  clean(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<CleanResult>;
  resolve<K extends keyof CapabilityConfigMap>(
    name: K,
    config?: CapabilityConfigMap[K]
  ): ResolvedCapability;
  isKnownCapability(name: string): name is keyof CapabilityConfigMap;
  registryRows(): ReadonlyArray<RegistryRow>;
  requiredFiles(platform: "ios" | "android"): readonly string[];
};

Generator input types (src/plugins/project/generators/types.ts — verbatim):

export type GeneratorInput = {
  global: Readonly<Config>;
  target: Target;
  capabilities: readonly ResolvedCapability[]; // resolved from config.system, platform-filtered
};

export type Artifact = {
  path: string;    // relative to projectDir, e.g. "src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
  content: string;
};

Behavior:
- generate({ target }): resolves config.system against the registry (unknown names throw),
  filters rows to those whose platforms include the target, runs the five generators
  (tauri-conf, cargo, rust, capabilities, sidecar), writes each artifact via write-if-changed
  under projectDir. Desktop targets get the whole tree; mobile targets get the shared tree +
  conf (the gen/ tree itself is created by `tauri ios|android init`, never by this plugin).
- completeness({ target }): mobile gen/<platform> required-file-set gate. Desktop => "not-applicable".
- patchMobile({ target }): idempotent post-init patch. v1 scope: Android signing state only
  (keystore.properties + a sentinel-delimited build.gradle.kts signing block). iOS is a documented no-op.
- clean({ target? }): mobile target => gen/<platform> only; desktop target => that target's
  bundle output; omitted => the whole projectDir. Every candidate path is validated against
  projectDir before deletion.
- resolve(name, config?): typed registry lookup; throws when name isn't in the registry, or
  when resolving "deep-link" without a non-empty scheme.
- onInit: validateProjectConfig(ctx.global) — see section 12.

Capability registry rows (registry.ts):
| name | npmPackage | platforms | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| store | @tauri-apps/plugin-store | all five | high |
| notification | @tauri-apps/plugin-notification | all five | high |
| clipboard-manager | @tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager | all five | high |
| tray | @tauri-apps/plugin-tray | macos, windows, linux (desktop only) | low (core Tauri feature modeled as a plugin-shaped row for registry uniformity) |
| deep-link | @tauri-apps/plugin-deep-link | all five | high (custom-scheme-only, D-011) |

v1 mobile permission codegen is conf-only (D-012): every registry row's sidecarPlist and
manifest arrays are EMPTY — official Tauri plugins self-merge their own AndroidManifest needs
via build.rs, and deep-link's iOS CFBundleURLTypes ride Tauri's own sidecar merge. The
Info.ios.plist sidecar (src-tauri root, OUTSIDE gen/ — never patch gen/apple/**/Info.plist)
is the pinned future iOS plist mechanism.

====================================================================
6. TAURI PLUGIN (Standard tier — src/plugins/tauri/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: the framework's ONLY @tauri-apps/cli subprocess seam — argv builders,
injectable spawn, process-group dev lifecycle, stream parsing, error taxonomy, secret
scrubbing. Invocation shape (D-013): [nodePath, tauriJsPath, verb, ...args] — explicit
PATH-walked real node binary against require.resolve("@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js").
Never `bunx tauri`, never --bun runtime, never the platform .node addon directly.
Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, argv.ts, resolve.ts, spawn.ts, dev.ts, stream.ts,
errors.ts, scrub.ts, state.ts.

Types (src/plugins/tauri/types.ts — verbatim):

/** Structural spawn seam — injectable for tests. */
export type SpawnFn = (opts: {
  cmd: readonly string[];
  cwd: string;
  env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  detached?: boolean;
  onLine?: (line: string) => void;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}) => Promise<{ code: number | null; signal: string | null; stdout: string; stderr: string }>;

/** tauri plugin per-plugin config — test seams. */
export type Config = {
  spawnImpl?: SpawnFn | undefined;
  nodePath?: string | undefined;
  readiness: { intervalMs: number; timeoutMs: number };
};

/** Result of a one-shot verb (non-zero exits throw TauriError instead). */
export type RunResult = { code: 0; stdout: string; stderr: string; durationMs: number };

/** Parsed compile progress tick — real crate counts, never fake percentages. */
export type CompileTick = { crate: string; index?: number; total?: number };

/** How a dev session ended. */
export type DevExit = { code: number | null; signal: string | null };

/** Live dev-session handle — teardown is owned HERE (D-002), never by cli. */
export type DevHandle = {
  url: string;
  ready: Promise<void>;
  exited: Promise<DevExit>;
  stop(): Promise<void>;
};

/** Classified subprocess failure taxonomy. */
export type TauriErrorKind =
  | "toolchain-missing"
  | "config-invalid"
  | "compile-failed"
  | "signing-failed"
  | "device-unavailable"
  | "cancelled"
  | "unknown";

/** Extra fields carried on a classified failure, alongside the standard `Error` shape. */
export type TauriErrorDetails = {
  readonly kind: TauriErrorKind;
  readonly exitCode: number | null;   // null when signal-terminated
  readonly stderrTail: string;        // scrubbed — safe to log/display
};

/** Thrown by every one-shot verb (icon/build/mobileInit) on a non-zero exit. */
export class TauriError extends Error implements TauriErrorDetails {
  readonly kind: TauriErrorKind;
  readonly exitCode: number | null;
  readonly stderrTail: string;
  constructor(kind: TauriErrorKind, message: string,
              details: { exitCode: number | null; stderrTail: string });
}

/** Mutable plugin state — the one live dev handle (undefined = no live session). */
export type State = { dev: DevHandle | undefined };

/** Public API of the tauri plugin — the framework's ONLY subprocess seam. */
export type Api = {
  icon(opts: { source: string }): Promise<RunResult>;
  build(opts: {
    target: Target;
    onTick?: (tick: CompileTick) => void;
    onOutput?: (line: string) => void;
  }): Promise<RunResult>;
  mobileInit(opts: { platform: "ios" | "android" }): Promise<RunResult>;
  dev(opts: { target?: Target; onOutput?: (line: string) => void }): Promise<DevHandle>;
  version(): Promise<{ cliVersion: string } | null>;
};

Behavior:
- icon({ source }): runs `tauri icon` from a source image. (v1 has no caller inside the
  framework — see D-015; the seam exists for a future Config.app.icon field.)
- build({ target, onTick?, onOutput? }): runs `tauri build` / `tauri ios|android build`.
  Every output line is scrubbed before reaching onOutput or a log. onTick receives parsed
  compile progress ("Compiling <crate> vX", optionally with cargo's [N/M] prefix). Throws a
  classified TauriError on non-zero exit.
- mobileInit({ platform }): runs `tauri ios|android init` — the ONLY init verbs exposed
  (plain `tauri init` is never used; the desktop tree is project-generated). NOT idempotent
  (tauri#13902) — callers must gate on project.completeness() === "not-initialized" first.
- dev({ target?, onOutput? }): starts the long-lived dev verb in a detached process group,
  installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers (group-kill + handler removal on exit), returns a DevHandle
  immediately. `ready` resolves from a devUrl readiness poll (config.readiness; no stdout
  "ready" marker exists — tauri#4740) and rejects (reaping the process group) on timeout.
  A second concurrent dev() call throws "[native] tauri dev already running". All dev output
  lines are scrubbed before onOutput/log. url = ctx.global.web.dev.url. stop() is idempotent.
- version(): probes CLI presence/version (used by doctor). Returns null when the CLI cannot
  be invoked — never throws.

Secret scrubbing (scrub.ts): known secret env-var names (APPLE_PASSWORD, APPLE_CERTIFICATE*,
TAURI_SIGNING_*, ...) are always masked; any other sufficiently long, high-entropy token is
masked too (Shannon entropy gate, not a fixed denylist). No output path bypasses the scrubber.

====================================================================
7. BUILD PLUGIN (Standard tier — src/plugins/build/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: the per-target packaging orchestrator. Runs scaffold -> codegen -> icons ->
compile -> bundle -> collect for one target, delegating scaffold/codegen to project and
icons/compile/bundle to tauri (ctx.require, D-007) — build never spawns a process itself.
Owns exactly one phase directly: collect. depends: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin]. No config,
no state, no onInit (validation is project's). Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts,
pipeline.ts, collect.ts.

Types (src/plugins/build/types.ts — verbatim, minus the local PluginLike helper):

/** Result of one target's full pipeline pass. */
export type BuildResult = {
  target: Target;
  outPath: string;
  artifacts: readonly string[];
  durationMs: number;
  phases: ReadonlyArray<{ phase: NativePhase; durationMs: number }>;
};

/** Public API of the build plugin — the per-target pipeline orchestrator. */
export type Api = {
  run(opts: { target: Target }): Promise<BuildResult>;
  runAll(opts?: { targets?: readonly Target[] }): Promise<readonly BuildResult[]>;
};

/** Domain context (structural): global + log + emit<Events> + require. */
export type BuildContext = {
  readonly global: Readonly<GlobalConfig>;
  readonly log: LogApi;
  readonly emit: EmitFn<Events>;
  readonly require: <P extends PluginLike>(plugin: P) => PluginApiOf<P>;
};

Phase semantics (pipeline.ts):
| Phase | Delegate | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| scaffold | project + tauri | Desktop: mkdir -p projectDir. Mobile: project.completeness() gate — "not-initialized" runs tauri.mobileInit() ONCE then re-checks; "incomplete" fails fast with a [native] fix-it pointing at `native doctor` / `native clean --target <t>` — a partial tree is never silently re-initialized. |
| codegen | project.generate() | Write-if-changed artifacts; mobile additionally project.patchMobile() (idempotent, every build — Android signing only in v1). |
| icons | (none in v1) | Permanent v1 no-op (D-015): no icon-source config field exists anywhere, so runIcons() always reports status "done", detail "skipped" — never guesses a source path. |
| compile | tauri.build() | ONE subprocess covers compile+bundle. compile carries the live onTick progress stream (native:phase "progress" with detail "Compiling <crate> i/total"). |
| bundle | (same subprocess) | Duration derived from the first scrubbed output line matching /bundling/i; zero-duration fallback when absent. A failure is ALWAYS attributed to compile; bundle is never emitted on failure. |
| collect | own (collect.ts) | Locates artifacts via BUNDLE_LOCATIONS, copies to outDir/<target>/. ZERO matches is an error — never a silent empty success. |

BUNDLE_LOCATIONS (collect.ts) — per-target glob patterns, resolved against bundleRoot():
  macos:   ["bundle/dmg/*.dmg", "bundle/macos/*.app"]        (root: src-tauri/target/release/)
  windows: ["bundle/nsis/*-setup.exe", "bundle/msi/*.msi"]   (root: src-tauri/target/release/)
  linux:   ["bundle/appimage/*.AppImage", "bundle/deb/*.deb", "bundle/rpm/*.rpm"]
  ios:     ["gen/apple/build/**/*.ipa"]                      (root: src-tauri/)
  android: ["gen/android/app/build/outputs/**/*.{aab,apk}"]        (root: src-tauri/)
Copies use fs.cp(..., { recursive: true }) so a macOS .app bundle (a directory) and
single-file installers copy through the same call.

runAll({ targets? }): sequential for every target (default ctx.global.targets) — NEVER
Promise.all: all five targets share one Cargo target/ lock, so parallelism would only
contend. Stops at the first failing target (no partial-continue in v1).

====================================================================
8. DOCTOR PLUGIN (Complex tier — src/plugins/doctor/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: diagnoses whether a target is actually buildable — toolchain presence,
mobile gen/-tree completeness, npm-vs-crate version skew, signing env-var presence, and
warn-only cross-repo pointers. depends: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin]. Declares and emits
doctor:check. Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, report.ts, checks/ (ten check modules +
registry + shared types).

Types (src/plugins/doctor/types.ts — verbatim, minus the local PluginLike helper):

/** Structural probe seam — injectable for tests. */
export type ProbeFn = (
  cmd: string,
  args: readonly string[]
) => Promise<{ code: number; stdout: string }>;

/** doctor plugin per-plugin config. */
export type Config = {
  probeImpl?: ProbeFn | undefined;
};

/** One completed check — also the doctor:check event payload. */
export type CheckResult = {
  id: string;
  target: Target | "host";
  status: "pass" | "warn" | "fail";
  message: string;
  fixIt?: string;
};

/** Aggregated diagnosis report (warns don't flip ok; fails do). */
export type DoctorReport = {
  ok: boolean;
  checks: readonly CheckResult[];
};

/** Events this plugin declares. */
export type DoctorEvents = {
  "doctor:check": CheckResult;
};

/** Public API of the doctor plugin. */
export type Api = {
  run(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<DoctorReport>;
};

Check interface (src/plugins/doctor/checks/types.ts — the providers pattern):

export type FsFacade = { readFile(path: string): Promise<string> };
export type CheckProjectApi = Pick<ProjectApi, "requiredFiles" | "completeness" | "registryRows">;
export type CheckTauriApi = Pick<TauriApi, "version">;

export type CheckInput = {
  target: Target | "host";
  global: Readonly<GlobalConfig>;
  probe: ProbeFn;      // doctor's own seam — never tauri's
  fs: FsFacade;
  env: EnvApi;         // presence only for signing (env.has, never env.get into messages)
  project: CheckProjectApi;
  tauri: CheckTauriApi;
};

export type Check = {
  id: string;
  appliesTo(target: Target | "host", global: Readonly<GlobalConfig>): boolean;
  run(input: CheckInput): Promise<CheckResult>;
};

The checks/ registry:
| Module | Diagnoses | Posture |
|---|---|---|
| rustup.ts | rustup present; the target's required rust triple installed | fail |
| node.ts | a real node binary on PATH, distinct from bun (tauri#9939) | fail |
| xcode.ts | Xcode/xcodebuild present, simulators queryable (ios, macOS host only) | fail |
| android.ts | ANDROID_HOME/SDK, NDK, JDK presence (android) | fail |
| signing.ts | signing env-var PRESENCE (never values) — Apple vars for ios/macos, signing.android.keystorePasswordEnv for android | warn |
| completeness.ts | mobile gen/ required-file-set via project.completeness(); fix-it is `native clean --target <t>` | fail (not-initialized = pass) |
| versions.ts | @tauri-apps/* npm major version vs. the registry-pinned crate range | warn only |
| web-script.ts | web.build/web.dev.command scripts exist in the SAME cwd Tauri will use (web.cwd honored); never executes the script | fail |
| tauri-cli.ts | CLI invokable via tauri.version() — the one probe routed through tauri | fail |
| cross-repo.ts | worker CORS must allow tauri://localhost / http://tauri.localhost (always fires); deep-link .well-known pointer (fires only when deep-link is composed) | warn only, always |

Behavior (api.ts):
- run({ target }) => every check whose appliesTo(target, global) is true, for that one scope.
- run() => every check for each of config.targets, PLUS every host-scoped check once
  (scopes = [...ctx.global.targets, "host"]).
- All scheduled (check, scope) pairs run in parallel via Promise.allSettled. A rejected
  check becomes an internal-error "fail" CheckResult (report.ts toCheckResult) — one broken
  check can never sink the report; run() itself only throws on an orchestration bug.
- Each completed result is emitted as doctor:check, then aggregated: ok === no "fail" rows.

====================================================================
9. CLI PLUGIN (Standard tier — src/plugins/cli/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: the consumer-facing verb layer — typed API methods, NO argv parsing.
Every output line flows through the branded kit @moku-labs/common/cli (MC1:
createBrandConsole, box, spinnerFrameAt, styled confirm) — never raw console.*
(test-enforced via spy). depends: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin].
Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, handlers.ts, render.ts, state.ts.

Types (src/plugins/cli/types.ts — verbatim, minus the local PluginLike helper):

/** Structural render sink — injectable for tests (default: branded console). */
export type RenderFn = (line: string) => void;

/** Structural confirm seam — injectable for tests (default: styled confirm). */
export type ConfirmFn = (question: string) => Promise<boolean>;

/** cli plugin per-plugin config. */
export type Config = {
  renderImpl?: RenderFn | undefined;
  confirmImpl?: ConfirmFn | undefined;
};

/** Live-render bookkeeping for the current verb invocation. */
export type State = {
  progress: { phase: NativePhase | undefined; startedAt: number | undefined; ticks: number };
};

/** Public API of the cli plugin — typed verbs, NO argv parsing. */
export type Api = {
  build(opts?: { target?: Target; all?: boolean }): Promise<void>;
  dev(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<void>;
  doctor(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<boolean>;
  clean(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<void>;
};

Behavior (api.ts):
- build(opts?): one target (default: the host target — darwin->macos, win32->windows,
  linux->linux via hostTarget(); mobile targets are NEVER inferred; unknown host platform
  throws a [native] error) or every configured target with { all: true } (ignores target).
  Delegates to build.run/build.runAll; progress renders live via the hooks.
- dev(opts?): awaits tauri.dev(...) handle's `ready` then `exited`, forwarding scrubbed
  output lines to the render seam. It NEVER stores the handle and NEVER calls stop() (D-002).
  A signal-terminated exit (code: null — e.g. Ctrl-C -> tauri's SIGINT group-kill) is the
  NORMAL way a dev session stops and resolves cleanly; only a numeric non-zero exit code
  throws "[native] tauri dev exited with code N".
- doctor(opts?): delegates to doctor.run, renders the final summary table with fix-its
  (live rows render via the doctor:check hook), returns report.ok — the CONSUMER SCRIPT
  sets process.exitCode.
- clean(opts?): thin delegate to project.clean (D-006). Without a target, the full
  projectDir wipe is gated behind a styled confirm ("Delete the entire native project
  directory (<projectDir>)? ..."); declining resolves without deleting anything.

hostTarget signature (exported from cli/api.ts, not the package root):
  function hostTarget(platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): Target

Hooks (handlers.ts, type CliHandlers): "native:phase", "native:complete", "doctor:check" —
see section 4. Live-render bookkeeping lives in ctx.state.progress (not closure variables);
undefined marks "no active phase" (D-014).

====================================================================
10. PUBLIC EXPORTS (src/index.ts + src/plugins/index.ts)
====================================================================

import {
  // Plugin instances
  projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin, cliPlugin,
  // Per-plugin type namespaces (each is the plugin's whole types module)
  Project, Tauri, Build, Doctor, Cli,
  //   e.g. Project.Api, Project.RegistryRow, Tauri.DevHandle, Tauri.TauriError (class),
  //        Build.BuildResult, Doctor.DoctorReport, Doctor.CheckResult, Cli.RenderFn
  // Shared constants
  TARGETS, PHASE_ORDER,
  // Shared types
  type CapabilityConfigMap, type Config, type Events,
  type NativeCompleteEvent, type NativePhase, type NativePhaseEvent,
  type SigningConfig, type Target,
  // Framework API
  createApp,     // Layer-3 factory: createApp({ config?, plugins?, pluginConfigs? })
  createPlugin   // consumer-plugin factory bound to this framework's Config/Events chain
} from "@moku-labs/native";

Framework-level pluginConfigs defaults (set in src/index.ts createCore call; every value
overridable per-app via createApp({ pluginConfigs })):
  tauri:  { spawnImpl: undefined, nodePath: undefined, readiness: { intervalMs: 250, timeoutMs: 60_000 } }
  doctor: { probeImpl: undefined }
  cli:    { renderImpl: undefined, confirmImpl: undefined }

====================================================================
11. USAGE EXAMPLES
====================================================================

--- The two-createApp consumer composition (D-009) ---

A native app is a SEPARATE createApp composed BESIDE the consumer's web/node app. Plugins
are bound to their own framework's factory chain, so native plugins can never join the web
app's plugin array — the two apps integrate at the edges.

// src/system.ts — the shared system-plugin composition: the cross-team contract.
// Both the web app and the native app import this SAME array; native codegens the entire
// permission surface from it.
export const systemPlugins = [
  { name: "store" },
  { name: "notification" },
  { name: "deep-link" }
];

// src/native.ts — the native createApp (Layer 3), beside your web app entry
import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/native";
import { systemPlugins } from "./system";

export const native = createApp({
  config: {
    app: { name: "MyApp", identifier: "com.example.myapp" },
    web: {
      build: "bun run build",
      dev: { command: "bun run dev", url: "http://localhost:5173" },
      dist: "dist"
    },
    system: systemPlugins,
    capabilities: { "deep-link": { mode: "scheme", scheme: "myapp" } }
  }
});

// package.json — thin per-verb consumer scripts (no argv CLI exists)
// {
//   "scripts": {
//     "native:dev": "bun run scripts/native-dev.ts",
//     "native:build": "bun run scripts/native-build.ts",
//     "native:doctor": "bun run scripts/native-doctor.ts",
//     "native:clean": "bun run scripts/native-clean.ts"
//   }
// }

// scripts/native-build.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.build({ target: "macos" }); // installers -> dist-native/macos/
await native.stop();

// scripts/native-dev.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.dev();          // resolves when the dev session exits (Ctrl-C is a clean exit)
await native.stop();

// scripts/native-doctor.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
const ok = await native.cli.doctor();
await native.stop();
if (!ok) process.exitCode = 1;   // the consumer script owns the exit code

// scripts/native-clean.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.clean();        // no target => confirm-gated full projectDir wipe
await native.stop();

Directory roles (gitignore both):
  .moku/tauri/   (projectDir) — the generated Tauri project: gitignored, fully regenerable,
                 never committed. Contains src-tauri/ with tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml,
                 Rust sources, capability JSON, and (after mobileInit) gen/apple|android.
  dist-native/   (outDir) — final packaged artifacts, per target: dist-native/macos/,
                 dist-native/android/, ...

--- Lower-level surfaces (everything cli fronts stays reachable) ---

await native.start();
await native.doctor.run({ target: "ios" });                  // DoctorReport
await native.project.generate({ target: "macos" });          // GenerateResult
const report = native.project.completeness({ target: "android" });
const result = await native.build.run({ target: "macos" });  // BuildResult
const all = await native.build.runAll();                     // sequential, config.targets order
const v = await native.tauri.version();                      // { cliVersion } | null
await native.stop();

--- Observing build progress from your own code ---

const results = await native.build.runAll({ targets: ["macos", "windows"] });
for (const r of results) {
  console.log(r.target, r.outPath, r.artifacts, r.durationMs, r.phases);
}
// Or hook the global events from a consumer plugin — see section 13.

--- Test seams (all subprocess/render/probe seams injectable) ---

import { createApp, type Tauri, type Doctor, type Cli } from "@moku-labs/native";

const lines: string[] = [];
const app = createApp({
  config: { /* ...valid app/web/system config... */ },
  pluginConfigs: {
    tauri: { spawnImpl: fakeSpawn, nodePath: "/usr/bin/node" },  // Tauri.SpawnFn
    doctor: { probeImpl: fakeProbe },                            // Doctor.ProbeFn
    cli: { renderImpl: line => lines.push(line), confirmImpl: async () => true }
  }
});
// The whole suite runs without any native toolchain installed.

====================================================================
12. ERROR HANDLING PATTERNS (as implemented)
====================================================================

House format: every framework error message is "[native] <what happened>." followed by an
indented actionable second line ("  <fix-it / next command>").

(a) Composition-time validation — project.onInit -> validateProjectConfig(ctx.global) throws:
  - "[native] app.name is required." (empty name)
  - '[native] app.identifier "<x>" is not a valid reverse-DNS identifier.'
  - "[native] web.build is required." / web.dev.command / web.dev.url / web.dist (each checked)
  - unknown config.system capability names (assertKnownCapabilities / unknownCapabilityError)
  - '[native] deep-link is composed in config.system but capabilities["deep-link"].scheme is
    missing.' — deep-link requires { mode: "scheme", scheme: "yourscheme" }.
  These fire at createApp composition, BEFORE any verb runs. Single owner: only project
  validates; build/doctor/cli have no onInit.

(b) Subprocess failures — tauri one-shot verbs (icon/build/mobileInit) throw TauriError:
  classify(code, scrubbedStderr) matches ordered, most-specific-first regex patterns over
  the ALREADY-SCRUBBED stderr:
    signing-failed:     /codesign|provisioning profile|keychain|signtool|jarsigner|keystore/i
    toolchain-missing:  /command not found|xcode-select|android_home|ndk (not found|is not installed)|rustup|cargo: not found/i
    device-unavailable: /no devices found|device not found|simulator (not booted|not found)|no emulators found|adb: no devices/i
    config-invalid:     /tauri\.conf|failed to parse .*config|invalid config|schema validation failed/i
    compile-failed:     /error\[e\d+\]|could not compile|compilation failed/i
  No match: kind = "cancelled" when exit code is null (signal-terminated), else "unknown".
  The error carries: kind, exitCode (number | null), stderrTail (last 20 non-empty scrubbed
  lines), and a message of the form "[native] tauri <kind with spaces>.\n  <per-kind advice>"
  (e.g. compile-failed => "Inspect the compile errors above; fix the source and retry.").
  classify never sees raw stderr — scrub first is the contract.

(c) Pipeline failures — build:
  - Each phase runs through a generic runner that emits native:phase "error" (with
    durationMs + the error message as detail) and RETHROWS; the next phase never starts
    (no partial-continue). runAll stops at the first failing target.
  - Mobile scaffold gate: an "incomplete" gen/ tree throws
    "[native] <target> project tree is incomplete.\n  Missing <files> — run `native doctor`
    to diagnose, or `native clean --target <t>` to reset before rebuilding."
    A partial tree is NEVER silently re-initialized (tauri#13902 can leave one).
  - collect: zero glob matches throws (never a silent empty success).

(d) Diagnosis — doctor.run never throws on check failures: Promise.allSettled + a
  settled-rejection -> internal-error "fail" CheckResult mapping (report.ts). Warns never
  flip report.ok; only "fail" rows do.

(e) Dev sessions:
  - tauri.dev(): concurrent second call throws "[native] tauri dev already running";
    readiness-poll timeout rejects `ready` and reaps the process group.
  - cli.dev(): a signal-terminated exit ({ code: null }) resolves cleanly (Ctrl-C is the
    normal stop); a numeric non-zero code throws "[native] tauri dev exited with code N.\n
    Check the rendered output above for the underlying error."

(f) Destructive operations — cli.clean() with no target requires a styled confirm before
  the full-projectDir wipe; declining resolves without deleting. project.clean validates
  every candidate path against projectDir before deletion.

(g) Secrets — signing config holds env-var NAMES, not values; doctor's signing check uses
  env.has only; every subprocess output line (build, dev, errors' stderrTail) passes the
  entropy-gated scrubber before any log/callback/exception.

====================================================================
13. EXTENSION PATTERNS (custom plugins)
====================================================================

The package root exports `createPlugin` — the consumer-plugin factory bound to this
framework's Config/Events chain. Consumer plugins are passed to createApp({ plugins: [...] }).
Every plugin ctx carries ctx.log and ctx.env (core plugins from @moku-labs/common).

(a) Hook the GLOBAL events — no depends edge needed (they're declared in the framework's
    Events type):

import { createApp, createPlugin } from "@moku-labs/native";
import type { NativeCompleteEvent, NativePhaseEvent } from "@moku-labs/native";

const notifyPlugin = createPlugin("notify", {
  hooks: ctx => ({
    "native:phase": (payload: NativePhaseEvent) => {
      if (payload.status === "error") ctx.log.warn("notify:phase-failed", { ...payload });
    },
    "native:complete": (payload: NativeCompleteEvent) => {
      ctx.log.info("notify:built", { target: payload.target, outPath: payload.outPath });
    }
  })
});

const native = createApp({ plugins: [notifyPlugin], config: { /* ... */ } });

(b) Hook a PER-PLUGIN event — needs the depends edge for event-type merging (this is the
    exact pattern the framework's own integration tests use):

import { createPlugin, doctorPlugin, type Doctor } from "@moku-labs/native";

const auditPlugin = createPlugin("audit", {
  depends: [doctorPlugin],
  hooks: () => ({
    "doctor:check": (payload: Doctor.CheckResult) => {
      // record/forward each completed check
    }
  })
});

(c) Call upstream APIs — depends + ctx.require:

import { createPlugin, buildPlugin, projectPlugin } from "@moku-labs/native";

const releasePlugin = createPlugin("release", {
  depends: [projectPlugin, buildPlugin],
  api: ctx => ({
    async ship(target: "macos" | "windows" | "linux") {
      const result = await ctx.require(buildPlugin).run({ target });
      ctx.log.info("release:shipped", { artifacts: result.artifacts });
      return result;
    }
  })
});
// createApp({ plugins: [releasePlugin] }) => app.release.ship("macos")

(d) Emitting the global events from your own plugin is sanctioned (spec/07 §6 / spec/14 §4:
    framework-domain:* events are emit/listen for any plugin), but in this framework build
    is the sole emitter by convention — prefer plugin-prefixed custom events for your own
    domains ("myplugin:thing"), declared via the register callback as doctor does.

(e) House patterns worth copying from the source:
    - Per-plugin domain context types are STRUCTURAL (global/config/state/log/env/emit/require
      picked per need), not the kernel's full PluginContext; build/doctor/cli re-derive a
      local PluginLike mirror for typed ctx.require.
    - Injectable seams (spawnImpl/probeImpl/renderImpl/confirmImpl) with `undefined` meaning
      "the real implementation" keep 90% coverage reachable without native toolchains.
    - State uses `undefined` for absence (never null), except where a union mirrors a Node
      API surface (DevExit.code/signal, version()'s | null) — D-014.
    - `| undefined` is spelled explicitly on optional config fields (exactOptionalPropertyTypes).

====================================================================
14. KEY DESIGN DECISIONS (from .planning/decisions.md)
====================================================================

- D-001: Tiers — project and doctor are Complex (generators/ and checks/ sub-domains);
  tauri, build, cli are Standard.
- D-002: tauri has NO onStop; dev teardown is owned by the dev seam's API control flow
  (process-group spawn, signal handlers, DevHandle.stop()). cli.dev awaits, never holds.
- D-003: native:phase / native:complete are GLOBAL framework events declared in config.ts,
  emitted by build, hooked by cli; doctor:check stays per-plugin.
- D-004: Shared types (Target, NativePhase, PHASE_ORDER, CapabilityConfigMap) live in
  src/config.ts; config.ts never imports from plugin directories.
- D-005: The substantive config surface is GLOBAL Config (app, web, system, capabilities,
  targets, projectDir ".moku/tauri", outDir "dist-native", signing env-var refs); per-plugin
  configs are minimal knobs.
- D-006: project owns clean (the generated tree's whole lifecycle); cli.clean is a thin,
  confirm-gated delegate.
- D-007: Dependency directions — build -> [project, tauri]; doctor -> [project, tauri];
  cli -> [project, tauri, build, doctor]; project and tauri stay dependency-free.
- D-009: The two-createApp consumer shape (separate src/native.ts beside the web app,
  shared src/system.ts contract, thin per-verb scripts, .moku/tauri + dist-native roles)
  is a documented deliverable — see section 11.
- D-011: deep-link is custom-scheme-only in v1 ({ mode: "scheme", scheme }); universal/app
  links deferred (no upstream entitlements write path); the mode discriminant keeps
  "universal" additive.
- D-012: v1 mobile permission codegen is conf-only — zero XML patching ships; patchMobile =
  Android signing state only; the Info.ios.plist sidecar (src-tauri root, outside gen/) is
  the pinned future iOS mechanism.
- D-013: tauri CLI invocation is [nodePath, tauriJsPath, verb, ...args] with a PATH-walked
  real node and require.resolve("@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js"); never bunx/`--bun`/the .node
  addon; node is a hard doctor prerequisite; plain `tauri init` is never used.
- D-014: State nullability — `undefined` is the house norm for absence; `| null` only
  mirrors Node API surfaces. tauri.dev() carries an onOutput render seam for cli.
- D-015: The icons phase is a permanent v1 no-op passthrough — no icon-source config field
  exists anywhere, so tauri.icon() has no framework caller and build's icons phase always
  reports done/"skipped". Revisit when a Config.app.icon (or similar) field ships.

Per-plugin READMEs (deeper narratives): src/plugins/project/README.md,
src/plugins/tauri/README.md, src/plugins/build/README.md, src/plugins/doctor/README.md,
src/plugins/cli/README.md. Moku Core specification:
https://github.com/moku-labs/core/tree/main/specification
